headline: The US open steadies the chips, but it doesn't reset the day
tone: Mixed at the US open: Nasdaq buyers are stepping back into the beaten-up chip names ahead of Nvidia tonight, while the Dow and Europe stay on the back foot. One afternoon bounce doesn't undo the three-day AI sell-off yet.
body: The bounce is narrow and it's in AI hardware. Marvell, AMD and Micron led the premarket recovery, and optical names like Coherent and Lumentum jumped after Reuters reported the administration will press ahead with blocking Chinese data-centre equipment, which helps US suppliers. Nvidia also set up a new board committee on national security, an attempt to calm the governance worries since Jensen Huang's exit.

The 14:30 data didn't change the picture. October retail sales rose 0.2%, exactly as forecast, but the control group that feeds GDP rose 0.6% against 0.4% expected, while car and furniture spending fell. Consumers are still spending, just picking more carefully, so nothing here argues against the Fed's hawkish lean ahead of Waller, Hammack and Williams later today.

The Dow is the weak spot because of company news, not the economy. Home Depot beat but trimmed its full-year outlook and named CFO Richard McPhail as CEO, and Disney slipped premarket despite a beat. Europe closes without the chip relief, so the morning's ASML, STMicro and Deutsche Bank losses mostly stand.

Crude firmed this afternoon on more tanker strikes near Hormuz, an Iranian drone attack on a US radar site in Bahrain and expectations of a US stock draw. The bigger force is still the surplus as Gulf exports return, which is why the strikes lift crude only at the margin. What would change the tone: Nvidia guidance after the close. A clean beat would turn this bounce into a proper relief rally; a soft guide would send chips back to their lows into Anthropic's listing on Thursday.

views.text: Priced in at the open: a relief bid in chips that depends entirely on Nvidia tonight, with Dow names held back by Home Depot and Disney. Europe has no Nvidia hedge left before its close, so any rebound there waits until tomorrow.

Solid core retail sales keep the case for further Fed hikes alive. Three Fed speakers this afternoon matter more for the dollar than the headline print, and the API crude stocks data at 21:30 Zurich is the next test for oil.
